problem: Existing indoor robot maps are mostly metric (occupancy grid) maps that lack object semantics, so humans cannot give intuitive object-level commands and the robot cannot ground them in the map.
motivation: Intuitive human-robot interaction requires the robot to understand objects in the environment and navigate to them. Linking a 3D object semantic map to a 2D occupancy grid lets object-level commands be converted into navigation goals on the grid.
key_idea: Build a hybrid map that combines a 3D object semantic map (from ORB-SLAM2 and YOLOv3 detections with merged object point clouds and 3D bounding boxes) with a 2D occupancy grid map, so object commands map to grid goals.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations are known. The abstract suggests that object semantics can act as a bridge between human commands and metric navigation maps, and that a modular pipeline of SLAM, 2D detection, and multi-view point cloud fusion is enough for semantic navigation in real environments.
method: Pose and 3D mapping: ORB-SLAM2 provides continuous pose estimation and a 3D point cloud map.
2D object detection: YOLO v3 detects objects in key-frames.
Object point cloud fusion: object point clouds from multiple viewpoints are merged and a 3D bounding box is estimated for each object.
3D object semantic map: the estimated 3D objects together form the semantic map.
2D occupancy grid: the 3D point cloud map is projected onto a 2D plane.
Hybrid map: the semantic map and the occupancy grid are combined, so human commands referring to objects are converted into grid-map goals for autonomous navigation.
